sources.title: OpenGitOps principles v1.0.0
findings: Names four principles: desired state expressed declaratively; stored so it is versioned and immutable with complete history; pulled automatically by software agents; continuously reconciled by agents that observe actual state and try to apply the desired state.
sources.limits: Principles only; the page itself does not define desired state, drift or software agent.

sources.title: OpenGitOps glossary
findings: Desired state is the configuration needed to rebuild a system so its instances behave the same, usually without persistent application data.
Drift is actual state moving or having moved away from desired state; reconciliation brings actual state into line whenever they diverge, from drift or an intended change.
A declarative description states the wanted operating condition without the steps to reach it.
sources.limits: No entry for software agent or state seed at access time.

sources.title: Infrastructure As Code (Martin Fowler bliki)
findings: Keep all configuration code in source control so each change is recorded for audit and builds are reproducible.
Nobody should log into a server and make on-the-fly adjustments; such changes breed snowflakes and belong only to developing the definition code.
sources.limits: Short bliki entry; does not use the word drift.

sources.title: Snowflake Server (Martin Fowler bliki)
findings: A server made unique by accumulated manual tweaks is hard to rebuild, keep in sync across a cluster or mirror for testing; unrecorded changes pile up and upgrades cause unpredictable side effects.
sources.limits: Does not name configuration drift; the effects are described only.

sources.title: Phoenix Server (Martin Fowler bliki)
findings: A phoenix server is regularly burned down and rebuilt from source configuration to guard against configuration drift, meaning untracked ad hoc changes.
Re-syncing tools correct drift only in areas they manage; rebuilding catches drift anywhere; the author recommends using both.
sources.limits: Server-centric view from the configuration-management era.

sources.title: Immutable Server (Martin Fowler bliki)
findings: An immutable server is never modified after deployment, only replaced; changes go to the base image, are tested and rolled out, and per-instance differences come from outside metadata.
sources.limits: Assumes disposable instances with data kept on separate storage.

sources.title: Open Policy Agent documentation
findings: OPA decouples policy decision-making from enforcement: software sends structured input and receives a decision.
Policy is written as code in Rego, a declarative language over hierarchical data.
sources.limits: Vendor documentation of its own product.

sources.title: OPA policy testing
findings: Policy tests are ordinary Rego rules prefixed test_, run with opa test; a test that is undefined or not true fails, and --fail-on-empty fails a run that executes no tests.
sources.limits: Vendor documentation of its own product.

sources.title: OPA with Terraform
findings: The plan is exported as JSON (terraform plan --out, then terraform show -json) and Rego rules read resource_changes and their actions to return an allow or deny decision.
sources.limits: Worked example; thresholds shown are illustrative.

sources.title: OPA in CI/CD
findings: OPA supports policy-as-code guardrails in CI/CD to verify configurations and enforce organizational policy before code reaches production; Conftest is suggested for IaC files in git.
sources.limits: Does not cover policy testing or Terraform plan JSON.

sources.title: OpenTofu state storage and locking backends
findings: A backend stores state and provides locking; with a non-local backend state is generally not kept on disk, except a local copy after a failed write; not every backend supports locking.

sources.title: OpenTofu state locking
findings: State is locked automatically during any operation that could write it to protect against corruption; -lock=false is discouraged; force-unlock risks multiple writers and is only for releasing your own lock.

sources.title: OpenTofu plan command
findings: -out writes a plan file meant to be applied in automation and to be treated as sensitive; a plain plan is speculative and not meant to be applied.
-refresh-only syncs state with out-of-band changes; routine resource targeting can leave undetected configuration drift.

sources.title: OpenTofu sensitive data in state
findings: State holds all resource attributes, including secrets such as initial database passwords; local state is plain-text JSON; treat state as sensitive data.
sources.limits: OpenTofu-specific; says nothing about plan files.

sources.title: OpenTofu import
findings: Existing resources can be brought under management; import blocks can import several resources and be reviewed in the normal plan and apply workflow.
